F1: The date-override early return happens before the busy-time check, so busy slots within an override are accepted.
F2: The `find` rejects a slot if any working-hours row for that weekday does not contain its start.
F3: The first same-date override that does not contain a slot causes rejection before later override rows are checked.
F4: The duplication is a code-structure concern; the behavior defects it describes are covered by the other findings.
F5: The date comparison uses object identity and mixes server-local formatting with UTC, which can misclassify override days.
F6: Slots are already constrained to fit working hours in `getTimeSlots`, so this redundant end check does not establish a behavior defect.
F7: The override’s shifted minutes are applied to the unshifted invitee day, placing cross-midnight overrides on the wrong date.
F8: An omitted override timezone is passed to `.tz()` instead of falling back to the organizer timezone, allowing results to depend on the server’s local zone.
F9: Test redundancy and fixture mismatch are test-quality concerns, not behavior defects.
